meal.name: Healing-Mouth Sunday Dinner
meal.workflow_md:
## Menu Serves 3 adults · soup + adult salmon add-on for 2 · Total ~45 min · Active ~30 min A soft white bean and turkey soup adapted for a post-extraction healing mouth: smooth and lukewarm for the son's portion, textured and brightened with lemon, herbs and chili at the table for the two adults, with a parallel roast salmon add-on to make it a full dinner. No acid or chili enters the shared pot. - **Lemony White Bean Soup with Turkey & Spinach** — the shared base; son's portion blended & sieved, served lukewarm - **Roast Salmon Add-On** — adult-first, flaked over the two adult bowls; optional and plain for the son ## T-Minus Timeline
TimeAction
T-45Heat pot; sauté onion + carrot until soft and golden-edged (7–10 min).
T-35Add tomato paste + cumin (1 min); add turkey, garlic, ginger, salt. Cook to 165°F / 74°C (5–8 min).
T-27Add stock + beans; smash reserved third of beans. Simmer 15–20 min.
T-25Salmon into oven at 275°F / 135°C — roast 15–18 min; pull at 120°F / 49°C internal.
T-8Salmon out; rest 5 min on tray, then flake, discard skin.
T-7Add chopped spinach to soup; simmer ~5 min until fully collapsed.
T-2Off heat. Adjust salt + cumin only — no lemon in the pot.
T-0 (son)Ladle son's portion; blend smooth + sieve; cool uncovered to lukewarm before serving.
T-0 (adults)Finish adult bowls: lemon, herbs, olive oil, chili/pepper. Flake salmon on top.
## Failure Prioritisation If the window slips, the son's portion fails first — it must be both uniformly smooth and cooled to lukewarm before it is served. Protect that ahead of plating speed for the adults. ## Critical Path The soup base governs timing; the salmon is a parallel roast slotted into the soup's simmer window and is not on the critical path. If timing slips, hold the salmon (it is fine at room temperature within the 2-hour window) and protect the son's portion — it must be smooth and lukewarm before serving. Do not serve his portion hot to save time. ## Heat / Oven Sequencing Soup runs on one induction burner start to finish; salmon owns the Bosch oven at a single temperature (275°F / 135°C) — no oven transition required. The two run concurrently with no resource conflict. Spinach goes in only after the salmon is out, so final soup attention and salmon flaking do not compete. ## Holding Chain
ComponentHold StrategyMax HoldDrift RiskCorrective
Soup (pot)Off-heat, covered; lukewarm/room temp acceptable.2 hr out of fridge totalThickens as beans absorb; over-2-hr food-safety risk.Loosen with warm stock/water to ladling consistency. Refrigerate beyond 2 hr; reheat adult leftovers gently.
Son's portionBlended + sieved; cooled uncovered to lukewarm.Serve fresh-cooledSkin forms; serves too warm if rushed.Stir to break skin; do not serve until comfortable on the lip. Thin with a little stock if tightened.
SalmonFlaked, loosely covered at room temp.2 hr out of fridge totalDries / firms as it sits.Fold flaked salmon into warm soup to re-moisten; refrigerate beyond 2 hr.

dishes.name: Lemony White Bean Soup with Turkey & Spinach
dishes.summary: A gentle ground-turkey and cannellini soup thickened with smashed beans and finished with spinach, kept acid- and chili-free in the pot so it can be blended and sieved for a healing mouth while adults finish their bowls with lemon, herbs and chili at the table.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview A soft, savory white bean and turkey soup with partially smashed beans for body; lemon, herbs and chili are moved entirely to the table so the shared base stays gentle on healing extraction sites. Meal-level carve-out: the soup functions as a soft, single-register dish by design — no internal hard-texture contrast required, as the post-extraction context prohibits it. ## Yield & Timing Yield: 3 adults · Total: ~45 min · Active: ~30 min · No oven (stovetop) ## Prep Phase 1. Dice onion and carrot. *Carrot peeled — skin turns fibrous and works against the no-chew goal.* 2. Mince garlic; grate ginger. 3. Drain and rinse beans; set aside about one-third for smashing. 4. Thaw frozen spinach and squeeze out excess water firmly in a towel or sieve. *If using fresh instead: 5 oz / 140 g baby spinach, roughly chopped.* 5. Chop herbs; hold for the table. ## Active Cooking 1. Heat a large pot over medium-high, 1 min. Add olive oil; heat until it thins, ~30 sec. 2. Add onion and carrot. Sauté until very soft and browned at the edges, 7–10 min. *Edges golden, onion translucent and collapsing.* 3. Add tomato paste and cumin. Sauté until the paste darkens and smells caramelized, ~1 min. 4. Add turkey, garlic, ginger, and ¾ tsp salt. Break up with a spoon and cook through, 5–8 min. *Primary cue: 165°F / 74°C on a probe. Corroborating: no raw pink remaining; fond building on pot base.* 5. Add stock and beans; bring to a simmer. Smash the reserved third of beans against the side of the pot and stir in to thicken. Simmer 15–20 min until thickened and flavorful. 6. Add chopped spinach. Simmer until fully collapsed and silky, ~5 min. *Fully wilted, no structure remaining.* 7. Off heat. Taste and adjust salt and cumin only — no lemon in the pot. *Salt conservatively; the dish finishes at the table and the salmon carries its own seasoning.* 8. **Son's portion (default — blended & sieved):** ladle out 1–2 servings, blend with an immersion blender until silky, then pass through a fine sieve to remove bean skins and any turkey grit. Cool uncovered to lukewarm before serving. ## Holding & Assembly Soup is eaten lukewarm or at room temperature. Total time out of refrigeration — soup and salmon both — should not exceed 2 hours; refrigerate beyond that. The son's portion is served smooth and lukewarm-to-room-temperature, never hot — cool uncovered, stirring occasionally, until comfortable on the lip; no lemon, chili, or black pepper. Adult bowls are finished at the table with lemon, herbs, a thread of olive oil, and chili/pepper to taste, with salmon flaked on top. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
CriticalGround turkey undercooked — below 165°F / 74°C, food-safety risk. Probe under 165°F / 74°C; meat soft-pink in the thickest clumps.Continue cooking until 165°F / 74°C throughout. Not served until reached.
CriticalSon's portion served too hot — heat on raw extraction sites risks irritating the wound or dislodging the clot. Steam rising; warm-to-hot on the lip.Cool uncovered, stirring, until lukewarm-to-room-temperature. Do not serve until comfortable on the lip.
CriticalSon's portion too textured — bean skins, turkey grit, or spinach fiber can lodge in the sockets. Visible skins or fibers; not uniformly smooth.Blend longer; pass through a fine sieve. Do not serve until uniformly smooth.
MajorSoup over-reduces during simmer or holding — beans absorb liquid, base turns paste-thick rather than spoonable. Coats the spoon heavily, mounds rather than settles.Loosen with warm stock or water, a splash at a time, off heat, until it ladles cleanly. Re-check salt after.
## Adjustment Notes If the adult bowls read flat, it's almost always lemon or salt rather than more cumin — add lemon a teaspoon at a time off-heat. If the soup is too thick after holding, loosen with warm stock. The son's portion should taste mild and clean by design — correct only with a pinch of salt and a little stock to thin, nothing sharp.

dishes.name: Roast Salmon Add-On
dishes.summary: Skin-on salmon fillet roasted low at 275°F / 135°C and pulled at 120°F / 49°C for a soft, just-set flake, served flaked over the adult soup bowls.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Gently roasted salmon pulled early for a soft, just-set flake, flaked over the two adult bowls to turn the soup into a complete dinner. ## Yield & Timing Yield: 2 adults (optional plain share for the son) · Total: ~25 min · Active: ~5 min · Oven: 275°F / 135°C ## Prep Phase 1. Pat fillet dry; rub with olive oil and ½ tsp salt. 2. Hold at room temperature 15 min before roasting. ## Active Cooking 1. Heat oven to 275°F / 135°C. 2. Place salmon skin-side down on a lined tray. Roast until it flakes with gentle pressure and is just opaque at the thickest point — pull at 120°F / 49°C internal; carries to ~125°F / 52°C off-heat. About 15–18 min for a 1-inch fillet. *Flakes separate when nudged with a fork; center barely translucent at pull.* 3. Rest 5 min on the tray. Flake into large pieces, discarding skin. ## Holding & Assembly Adult-first add-on. Holds at room temperature within the same 2-hour out-of-fridge window. Flake over the two adult bowls at serving; lemon wedges are adult-only. Soft enough for the son if he'd like a little, kept plain and lemon-free — but flaky fish still needs some oral movement, so it's optional for him, not part of his core portion. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorSalmon overcooked — pulled past 125°F / 52°C, flesh dries and firms, losing the soft flake the healing context needs. Flakes chalky, no sheen.Unrecoverable for texture; dish remains serviceable. Fold flaked salmon into the warm soup so the broth re-moistens it.
## Adjustment Notes If the salmon firms or dries while holding, fold the flaked pieces into the warm soup so the broth re-moistens them; this also softens it further for the son's optional share.
